## Why each is what it is

- **TA-01** (consumes-resolution) — every job installs the runtime technology.lock.json resolves (the test lanes from ci.test, the browser and postgres jobs the runtime the production image carries); before PR-053 the workflow listed 22.13, 22 and 24 itself and let 22 and 24 float to whatever the runner cached
- **TA-02** (unverified-assumption) — the hosted runner label is the bootstrap; the provider moves it between image versions, so the image version is recorded as evidence (20261025.353.1 in run 40877050799), not pinned. scripts/technology.js check validates the label against the lock
- **TA-03** (consumes-resolution) — pinned to the commits their v5 tags pointed at (the same commits run 40877050799 downloaded); a workflow uses: line cannot be an expression, so the check validates each against the lock
- **TA-04** (consumes-resolution) — the PostgreSQL service image is the digest the lock resolves; it was the floating tag postgres:16
- **TA-05** (unverified-assumption) — the optional queue's image in the compose example: a floating tag, never exercised by CI (no test runs the Redis queue). Its current digest is in the discovery snapshot; resolving it needs a test that runs the queue
- **TA-06** (consumes-resolution) — a Dockerfile FROM cannot read a file a plain docker build does not pass in, so the base stays written and the check validates it against the deploy.container resolution (tag and digest)
- **TA-07** (technical-constraint) — the floor is derived: the highest `since` among the capabilities platform.runtime needs (node:sqlite unflagged, 22.13.0). The check fails when package.json says anything else
- **TA-08** (generated-resolution) — declared ranges; package-lock.json (npm's generated resolution, ingested by the npm-lockfile adapter) pins each release and its integrity, and its digest is part of the lock
- **TA-09** (technical-constraint) — the two built-in modules whose availability sets the runtime floor; each is a capability of the runtime item with the release it arrived in
- **TA-10** (technical-constraint) — core modules every release at or above the floor provides; a module not listed here is a new assumption the gate reports
- **TA-11** (adapter) — the optional queue and metrics adapters; each is loaded only when configured and resolved through package-lock.json
- **TA-12** (generated-resolution) — the development DOM the console suites drive; a devDependency resolved through package-lock.json
- **TA-13** (diagnostic) — names the runtime in a message or a status report; decides nothing (the boot guard probes for node:sqlite instead of comparing version numbers)
- **TA-14** (consumes-resolution) — verify-runtime compares the running runtime with the release the lock resolved for the lane
- **TA-15** (technical-constraint) — the web's own protocols, which the platform serves and calls
- **TA-16** (adapter) — the PostgreSQL adapter (lib/pg.js speaks the wire protocol; SQLite through node:sqlite is the default engine)
- **TA-17** (adapter) — the optional Redis queue adapter
- **TA-18** (technical-constraint) — the authenticator key URI format (otpauth://) and a placeholder in a message; not runtime technology
- **TA-19** (unverified-assumption) — the systemd units run the host's runtime; nothing checks that it is a resolved release (the boot guard still refuses one without node:sqlite)
- **TA-20** (technical-constraint) — the convenience scripts' shell
- **TA-21** (unverified-assumption) — the real-browser checks find Chrome or Chromium where the host put it (CHROME_PATH overrides); the CI runner image provides it unpinned, and the browser job now prints its version as evidence
